blockingFindings: On Windows, if the child closes before taskkill emits its outcome, the close handler cancels the settlement timer and immediately emits cancelled; a later taskkill failure is suppressed because the child is no longer running. This can report cancellation without confirming tree termination, violating fail-closed cancellation semantics.
missingNegativeTests: Add a deterministic test where the child-close event precedes taskkill spawn-error or nonzero completion, asserting cancellation-failed/failed terminal handling and no review persistence.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: The launcher separates context construction, assessment parsing, binding, persistence, progress, and cancellation into bounded functions, but cancellation completion ordering needs correction.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: Provider and production authority remain outside the runner; the local Codex child is isolated behind process-control and persistence adapters.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Structured progress events are generally well bounded and redacted, but Windows cancellation currently permits a terminal cancelled event before termination outcome confirmation.

exactNextAction: Make Windows cancellation await and record the taskkill outcome and child-close confirmation before emitting the terminal cancelled event; fail closed on either missing confirmation or termination failure, then add the ordering regression test.
